problem: Let $A(-1,3,2,-4)$, $B(1,0,1,-2)$, and $C(0,1,-1,2).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality and the Angle Between Two Vectors

feedback.problem: Let $A(1,1,-1,-1)$, $B(2,4,6,8)$, and $C(1,2,3,4).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0+3\cdot 1+7\cdot 4+9\cdot 5}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{9}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{5}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{76}{\sqrt{140}\cdot \sqrt{42}} \\  & =\frac{76}{2\sqrt{35}\cdot \sqrt{42}} \\  & =\frac{76}{14\sqrt{30}} \\  & =\frac{38}{7\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}
$$
